The System Control Plane

Plane 0x11 — where codepoints are instructions.

The System Control Plane (SCP) occupies 0x110000–0x11FFFF. Its codepoints are machine instructions: they do not print and they do not advance the cursor. Every instruction in the kernel’s diagnostic machinery lives here.

The BANcode Registry

Block Range Role
BANcode (B+) 0x0011A000–0x0011A7FF Hard diagnostics — halt or rollback the stream
WARNcode (W+) 0x0011A800–0x0011ABFF Soft diagnostics — warn and continue
COMcode (C+) 0x0011AC00–0x0011ADFF Communication and datagram instructions
SOFTcode (S+) 0x0011AE00–0x0011AEFF Runtime / soft-fault instructions

The remaining SCP slots (0x110000–0x11A000 and 0x11AF00–0x11FFFF) are reserved for future registry blocks, exactly as the control plane of a processor reserves opcode space.

Dispatch

Diagnostics produced anywhere in the kernel are dispatched through the SCP. The registry functions sucs_bancode_to_trap() and friends map a registry codepoint to the corresponding trap so a hard BANcode halts the stream while a WARNcode lets it continue.

BANcode 0x0011A0xx → trap 0x7FFFFFF0+ // hard: halt/rollback
WARNcode 0x0011A8xx → warn and continue // cursor advances

System and App modes

The dispatch path for a fatal B+ BANcode depends on the mode the registry runs in. Both modes share the identical codepoint registry.

  • System mode — the krnl path. Fatal BANcodes route to the Kernel Security Trap governing their 128-codepoint cluster (0x7FFFFFF0+slot); the fitted damage-control handler executes in the crash context.
  • App mode — application code. Fatal BANcodes bypass the traps entirely and are delivered to the App-level crash handler registered by the application (bancode_register_app_crash_handler()), so the krnl dispatch table is never entered.

Also see machine instructions, diagnostics, the BANcode Registry, and sudat/control/SCP.txt in the database.
